llm.summary: This is an offline AI-output provenance ledger, but it needs review because its metadata says no filesystem/subprocess permission while the documented tool writes persistent local registry files containing provenance data and output summaries.

dimensions.detail: The implementation is local, stdlib-only, and writes to ./registry, which is proportionate for a ledger. However, add stores the first 60 characters of the registered output in CSV/Markdown/JSONL, so sensitive content can be copied into durable side files.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The frontmatter declares permissions.network/filesystem/subprocess as false, but the skill also declares a Python CLI entry point, allowed Bash/Write tools, and a script that reads user-specified files and writes registry files. That metadata mismatch under-discloses the authority the skill actually needs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language includes broad terms such as '有籍', and the SKILL.md usage examples use --register/--verify flags while the actual Python CLI and schema use add/verify/lookup/report subcommands. This creates avoidable ambiguity for agents or wrappers invoking the tool.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is central to the purpose and is disclosed, but the registry is durable across runs, duplicated in three formats, and has no documented deletion, redaction, retention, or configurable storage controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core capability is coherent with the stated purpose: hash AI outputs, record model/version/prompt-hash/ownership metadata, and support add/verify/lookup/report. I found no network code, remote payload retrieval, destructive behavior, or credential handling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill creating a persistent local ledger under registry/. Do not register confidential outputs unless you accept that a short summary, model/version, ownership fields, hashes, and timestamps will be stored in JSONL, CSV, and Markdown. Review the permission metadata mismatch before relying on platform permission declarations.
llm.findings:
[SDI-3] unexpected: Confirmed a real metadata mismatch: SKILL.md says filesystem/subprocess permissions are false, while the CLI reads files and writes ./registry outputs. This supports Review, not maliciousness, because the behavior itself is purpose-aligned and documented elsewhere.
[SQP-2] expected: Confirmed local persistence of hashes, prompt hashes, ownership fields, and output summaries. This is expected for a provenance ledger, but the raw summary excerpt and lack of retention/redaction controls are user-relevant privacy concerns.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed documentation inconsistency between --register style examples in SKILL.md and the actual add/verify/lookup/report argparse interface. README and the input schema are closer to the real implementation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Confirmed broad trigger wording, including a very short standalone trigger. This is a routing quality concern that could cause unexpected activation, but I did not find hidden execution or automatic record creation.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-first documentation and registry labels are present, but SKILL.md includes English description and usage sections. I downgraded these language-only findings because they are not evidence of security abuse.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The README contains external badge/link URLs while claiming offline operation. I treated this as a documentation precision issue only; the runtime script itself has no network behavior.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Confirmed the timestamp string hardcodes +08:00. This can affect audit interpretation for users outside that timezone, but it is not evidence of malicious behavior.
